archetypes.name: path-resolver
archetypes.rationale: The plan prescribes four distinct source-library path forms per script; a mismatch between plan and each file's existing sourcing convention would silently resolve to the wrong (or missing) library.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check each script in the file list against the source-library path expression the plan prescribes for it (`$SCRIPT_DIR/lib-design-tmpdir.sh`, `$SCRIPT_DIR/../../../scripts/lib-design-tmpdir.sh`, `$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib-design-tmpdir.sh`, `$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib-design-tmpdir.sh`). For each script, read the existing source lines and verify the prescribed path form is consistent with how that script already resolves sibling libraries (e.g., if a script uses `$PLUGIN_ROOT` for lib-quiet.sh, the plan must also assign the `$PLUGIN_ROOT` form for the new source). Flag every script where the plan's prescribed form differs from the file's observed pattern, because a wrong form would silently resolve to a missing path on some invocation roots. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: variable-binding
archetypes.rationale: The plan names three different argv-bound variable names (DESIGN_TMPDIR, DESIGN_TMPDIR_ARG, design_tmpdir) across the 17 scripts; a misidentified binding would pass an empty or wrong value to the validator without error.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that the plan correctly identifies the variable name each script binds from `--design-tmpdir` argv parsing. The plan assigns `DESIGN_TMPDIR` to most scripts, `DESIGN_TMPDIR_ARG` to write-design-current-env.sh and render-plan-review-prompt.sh, and lowercase `design_tmpdir` to emit-design-plan-preview.sh. For each script in the file list, read the argv parser and confirm the variable the plan names matches what the script actually stores the `--design-tmpdir` value into at the point of the validate call. A mismatch would pass an empty or unrelated variable to `larch_design_tmpdir_validate` without any visible error. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: error-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan adapts only design-pause-load.sh away from `|| exit $?`; other scripts may have their own KV-output or exit-semantics contracts that a bare `|| exit $?` would silently violate.
archetypes.prompt_body: Identify every script in the file list that uses a non-standard error-reporting pattern — emit_fail, die_usage, KV output before exit, or exit-0-on-error contracts — and check whether the plan has correctly adapted the validate call for each one. The plan explicitly adapts design-pause-load.sh to use `emit_load_fail` instead of `|| exit $?`, but applies `|| exit $?` to all other scripts without verification. Read each script's error-handling conventions and caller contracts to determine if a bare `|| exit $?` on validation failure would break a downstream KV parser, skip required cleanup, or exit with an unexpected code that callers interpret differently. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
